messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s admitting they feel it too. The clinic’s stocking up, the banks are nervous, and even the shopkeepers are dropping hints like they’ve already made up their minds. Stay sharp, but keep it quiet—we don’t know who’s still holding the strings from the outside."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting underfoot, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the first tremors. The usual signals are flickering, but the lights are still on… for now. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to trip over our own feet."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are cracking—small things, but you can feel the draft. My boss is jumpy, the TV cut out for hours, and even the imam’s sermon last week had teeth. Something’s coming, but whether it’s a storm or just a bad wind, I don’t know yet. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s saying it out loud. The usual cracks are wider, and the silence from above is louder than any speech. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to move, just to watch."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels different—like the ground is shifting under our feet, but no one’s saying it out loud yet. Even the soldiers at the checkpoints seem to know something’s coming, and the silence from the palace speaks louder than any of their usual noise. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to move, just to watch."*"
Sender 6: "*"Things are shifting faster than we thought—small cracks, but they’re spreading. The regime’s still holding the line, but the way the air feels now? It’s like everyone’s waiting for the other shoe to drop, even if they’re pretending not to notice."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are cracking—quietly, but everywhere. The old hands are being pushed aside, the orders don’t make sense anymore, and even the kids at school aren’t paying attention. If the regime can’t keep its own people in line, it’s only a matter of time before the rest of us stop pretending too."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are sweating—everyone’s whispering about ‘how’ instead of ‘if,’ and the money men are already betting on the fall. But don’t mistake the stumble for the collapse yet; the old guard’s still got a few tricks left, and the streets might not be ready to push when the moment comes. Keep your ears open, your mouths shut, and your bags packed—just in case."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are cracking, but not falling—not yet. The guards are watching their own backs now, the money’s stuck, and the neighbors are talking louder than they used to. Still, the provinces don’t feel it, and the diplomats are just as lost as we are. Could be the start of something, or just another false dawn—either way, we’re in the quiet before the next move."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—payments are on time, but the backrooms are quiet, and the streets are testing limits without pushback. Something’s shifting, but whether it’s weakness or just the calm before a storm, we’d be fools to assume we know which way it’ll break."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels different—people are talking, but the market’s still full and the military’s still training. The cracks are there, but no one knows if they’ll split wide open or get papered over. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 12: "*"Things are holding, but just barely—like a dam with too many cracks. The elites are settling scores faster now, the military’s acting like they’re in this for the long haul, and even the traders are sweating but still playing along. But the little things? The way the intelligence parent bolted early, the way the ambulances showed up late and confused—those are the signs. We’re not there yet, but the ground’s shifting under us. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and keep an eye on the exits."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels different now—even the cautious ones are stepping forward, and the usual cracks in the system are widening faster than they can patch. The guards are hesitating, the borders are quiet, and the sermons are getting sharper, but the real question is whether the wolves will turn on each other before the storm hits."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are cracking—more than usual. The usual fixers are gone, the watchers are watching each other, and the money’s flowing like it’s supposed to, but the streets are quieter now. Not cold, just waiting. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t over, and we don’t know yet if it’s breaking or just bending."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting underfoot, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the wind. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could go either way."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels different now—not just quieter, but like something’s shifting under the surface. The usual signs are there: the clinic stocking up, the flights filling, even the palace acting like nothing’s wrong. But the real question isn’t if, it’s when—and whether we’ll be ready when it happens."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s admitting it yet. The usual rules don’t seem to apply anymore, and that’s either a warning or an opening. Stay sharp, but don’t do anything that can’t be explained away."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels different—checkpoints thinning, the bank scrambling, even the kids know the words now. The top is cracking, but no one’s sure if it’s the whole roof or just a few tiles. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could be the calm before the storm or just another false alarm. Let’s keep listening."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting under us, and not just for a few. Even the kids are singing what the adults whisper. The usual cracks are widening, and the regime’s messages sound like they’re trying to convince *themselves* more than us. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to move, just to watch. And if you hear from others, pass it quietly. We’ll know soon enough which way the wind breaks."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels lighter now—people are talking louder, even the sermons are sharper—but the clinic’s stocking extra bandages, and the security teams aren’t even pretending to be nervous. Either they’re so sure of themselves they don’t care, or they’re waiting for something we can’t see yet. Either way, we should be ready for both."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are thinner than we thought—people are talking louder, and the usual enforcers are looking the other way. Something’s shifting, but we don’t know yet if it’s a storm or just the calm before the next crackdown. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we need to see who blinks first."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for the next move. The regime’s still in charge, but the ground’s shifting under them, and no one’s sure which way it’ll go when it does."*"
Sender 23: "*"The ship’s listing bad—even the captains are whispering about it now. Keep your heads down, but don’t be surprised if the wind changes fast."*"
Sender 24: "*"Things are holding, but it feels like we’re all standing on a frozen lake—no one’s cracking the ice yet, but no one’s moving either. The regime’s still got its grip, but the quiet’s starting to feel like the kind before a storm, not the kind after."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are cracking—small things, but the kind that don’t get fixed. The usual channels are clogged, the sermons are sharper, and the silence from the stats office says more than the numbers ever did. Let’s keep our ears open, but quietly—no need to draw attention to the creaks."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
